Implement code in the git worktree /Users/itsmeyaw/projects/binden/.worktrees/issue-12-handover (branch issue-12/auto-handover, already checked out; stacked on issue-12/workspace-writes whose last 3 commits added the helpers below). Work ONLY in that directory. Read AGENTS.md there first (use shadcn + tailwind only, no manual CSS; check shadcn MCP/components already in src/components/ui before adding anything; Next.js version differs—check node_modules/next/dist/docs if touching Next APIs). Minimal diffs, match existing style (short "why" comments, `ponytail:` for known shortcuts). No new deps.

## Goal
When an administrator accepts a signup request, the app must (1) create the Workspace user (already done), (2) once provisioning completes, reset the user's password to a fresh temporary one with change-at-next-login, and (3) email the temporary password to the applicant's verified contact email via Gmail as the acting administrator. This replaces the manual Admin-console handover (open console → Reset password → email → come back and click "Confirm instructions were sent").

Available helpers (from the layer below; read them):
- src/lib/directory.ts: `resetWorkspacePassword(actor, userKey): Promise<string>` (PATCH password + changePasswordAtNextLogin; simulated under GOOGLE_SIMULATION=true), `Actor`.
- src/lib/gmail.ts: `sendMailAsActor(actor, { to, subject, text })` (no-op under GOOGLE_SIMULATION=true).
- src/lib/provisioning.ts: `provisionAcceptedRequest(id, actor)`, `retryProvisioning(id)`, `completeIfAllAdded`, `confirmHandover(id, adminDirectoryId)`, `reviseAssignment`, `getProvisioningProgress`.

## Tasks
1. src/lib/provisioning.ts: replace `confirmHandover` with `sendHandover(id: string, actor: Actor): Promise<"sent" | "already" | "blocked" | "unavailable">`:
   - In one `getDb().transaction`: `select ... for update` the request row (status, accountCreateState, googleUserId, workspaceEmail, contactEmail, givenName). Require the same conditions confirmConfirm used (status awaiting_handover, accountCreateState created, no signupRequestGroup with state != added — reuse the existing notExists condition shape). If not met, fall through to the existing already/blocked/unavailable classification.
   - Then `const password = await resetWorkspacePassword(actor, googleUserId)`, then `sendMailAsActor(actor, { to: contactEmail, subject: "Your Workspace account is ready", text })` where text greets by givenName, gives the Workspace email, the temporary password, says to sign in at https://accounts.google.com with the Workspace email and that Google will require choosing a new password at first sign-in, and that the temporary password stops working if a new one is sent. Then update status to "handover_confirmed", handoverConfirmedAt now, handoverConfirmedByDirectoryId actor.profile.id. Any throw rolls back, leaving awaiting_handover (retryable). Add a `ponytail:` comment: the row lock is held across the two Google calls so concurrent sends cannot mail two different passwords; fine at this scale. The password must never be persisted, logged, or put in mail_message.
   - After commit keep the existing best-effort `captureReviewerMail` notice, text changed to "A first-login email with a temporary password was sent to the applicant." (no applicant data).
   - Keep the DB status value `handover_confirmed` (indexes/migrations depend on it); do not add statuses or migrations.
   - `provisionAcceptedRequest(id, actor)` and `retryProvisioning(id, actor)` (new actor param): after `completeIfAllAdded`, call `sendHandover(id, actor)` inside try/catch (a mail/reset failure must not fail the accept/retry; the request stays awaiting_handover and the admin can resend). Also, `reviseAssignment` can complete provisioning? Check whether any other path moves to awaiting_handover (grep for completeIfAllAdded / "awaiting_handover"); if a route completes provisioning, trigger sendHandover there too with the route's `access`.
   - Update callers: acceptance route, provisioning retry route (src/app/api/review/requests/[id]/provisioning/route.ts), handover route (src/app/api/review/requests/[id]/handover/route.ts → calls `sendHandover(id, access)`; update comments and the "blocked" message to "The first-login email can be sent once every selected membership has succeeded.").
2. UI src/components/account-handover.tsx (and wherever it is rendered / the step labels like "Awaiting handover" / "Handover confirmed" live—find them, probably src/components/review-request.tsx): 
   - awaiting_handover now means "the first-login email has not been sent (yet or it failed)": show an Alert explaining that the email with a temporary password could not be sent to the applicant's contact email, and a button "Send first-login email" opening the existing AlertDialog: title "Send the first-login email?", description "This sets a new temporary password for {email} and emails it to the applicant's contact email. Any earlier temporary password stops working. It does not show that the message was delivered or that the applicant has signed in." Action button "Send email". Remove the Admin console link/steps and the now-unused props/vars (adminUrl/adminEmail) if nothing else uses them.
   - handover_confirmed label/text: "First-login email sent" plus that it records the email was sent with a temporary password, not that it was delivered or used. Keep the existing component structure; only change copy and remove the manual steps.
3. Tests:
   - tests/handover.ts and tests/provisioning.ts: update for sendHandover and new signatures. Under GOOGLE_SIMULATION=true, accepting a request with all groups succeeding should end in handover_confirmed automatically, with exactly one reviewer notice in mail_message and no password anywhere in mail_message/signup_request. Add a real-path block (GOOGLE_SIMULATION unset, using tests/fake-directory.ts which already records Directory writes and Gmail messages; read it): accept a request with no groups → users POST, then PATCH with a password, then one Gmail message to the contactEmail whose decoded body contains the same password as the PATCH body and the workspace email; status handover_confirmed. And a failure block: make Gmail fail (use/extend the fake's failure option) → accept still succeeds, status stays awaiting_handover; then `sendHandover` again with Gmail healthy → handover_confirmed, and the second PATCH password differs from the first. Concurrent `Promise.all([sendHandover, sendHandover])` → outcomes ["already","sent"] sorted and exactly one Gmail message.
   - tests/review.spec.ts (Playwright e2e, cannot run here—just keep it coherent and type-correct): accept-with-groups-all-succeeding now ends at handover_confirmed / "First-login email sent", not "Awaiting handover"; rewrite the manual-confirm test to cover resending via the "Send first-login email" button where reachable (e.g. seed a request directly in awaiting_handover state if the spec's seed helpers allow), and update the blocked/not-awaiting tests' expected messages. Adjust other expectations that assumed awaiting_handover after accept/retry/revise.
4. Docs: add docs/adr/0003-automated-account-handover.md (short, same tone as docs/adr/0001-*.md and 0002): accept creates the user with a throwaway password, and once memberships succeed the app resets it to a random temporary password with change-at-next-login and emails it to the verified contact email via Gmail as the acting administrator (admin grant gains gmail.send). Supersedes ADR 0001's "Admin console reset … rather than emailing a plaintext password" sentence and, for this message only, ADR 0002's dedicated-mailbox sender. State the trade-off honestly (a plaintext temporary password in email, mitigated by forced change at first sign-in and invalidation on resend; never stored by the app). Edit 0001 and 0002 minimally to point to 0003 at the superseded sentences. Update README / docs/live-workspace-smoke-check.md / CONTEXT.md only where they describe the manual handover (grep "handover", "Reset password", "Admin console").

## Verify & commit
In the worktree: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm exec next typegen` if needed then `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm test`. All must pass. Small commits in repo style (imperative sentence; see `git log --oneline -10`), e.g. (a) provisioning sendHandover + routes + unit tests, (b) UI + e2e spec, (c) ADR/docs. No Co-Authored-By trailers. Do NOT push.

Return: commits (hash + message), files changed, final sendHandover code, test results, and open concerns.

# Google is authoritative for Workspace users and administrative authority

This application serves one nonprofit's Google Workspace organization. Use Google-backed sign-in for existing Workspace users, Google Workspace administrative privileges for management authorization, and Google Workspace as the source of truth for existing user profiles and group membership, rather than maintaining parallel application-owned profiles or administrator roles.

The application stores signup requests separately because applicants do not yet have managed accounts. Signup uses verified contact email without requiring a personal Google account or an applicant dashboard. Workspace users may edit only their own permitted contact information; Workspace email, organizational assignments, group membership, account status, and security settings remain administrator-controlled. Administrators manage direct Workspace-user group membership, including member, manager, and owner roles; group roles alone do not grant application administration.

Suspension is the normal offboarding action. Deletion is a distinct, explicitly confirmed action after an administrator has resolved data disposition in Google's Admin console. Account handover uses the Admin console's existing-user password reset and email flow, with a required password change, rather than emailing a plaintext password.

Unreviewed signup requests expire after 30 days. Rejected applicant profiles are deleted after outcome notification; successful applicant form data is removed after provisioning and handover. Retain only a minimal operational record identifying the resulting Google account and approving administrator. Email verification evidence and pending workflow data may live in the application without becoming a second source of truth for the current Workspace profile.
# Use administrator OAuth and approved profile changes

Ordinary-user OAuth consent does not authorize Directory profile writes, even to the user's own account. For this small nonprofit, users submit verified contact email and phone changes for approval; the application executes approved changes and administrative operations using the acting administrator's OAuth credentials. Google therefore enforces that administrator's privileges and resource restrictions, without a shared stronger account or a parallel application role model.

Prefer this workflow over domain-wide delegation: Google's Directory user write scope is not limited to contact fields, and delegation scopes do not restrict which account a service account may impersonate. The trade-off is that contact changes wait for an authorized administrator instead of taking effect immediately. Domain-wide delegation can be reconsidered if that approval delay becomes unacceptable.

Request `admin.directory.user` for user management and `admin.directory.group` for group and membership management; add read-only role inspection only if required for the interface. Restrict profile change requests to contact email and phone, preserve unrelated Directory entries, and keep Workspace email, account recovery fields, and security settings outside that workflow. A new contact email must be verified before it can be approved. Do not retry denied operations using stronger credentials.

Send verification, outcome, and administrator notification emails through a dedicated Workspace mailbox with a separate offline OAuth grant limited to `gmail.send`. Notify a configured Google Group when a verified signup or profile change request is submitted, including a review-queue link and minimal personal information. The notification group's membership determines delivery only, never approval authority; configure it to accept mail from the sender.

Assume administrator-managed Directory/contact sharing is enabled and managed users are visible in the Directory. Read the signed-in user's own profile with their OAuth grant containing `admin.directory.user.readonly`, explicitly using `viewType=domain_public`. Resolve the target from the authenticated identity and return only that user's permitted shared fields. Omitted contact fields are unavailable, not evidence that the stored value is empty. Keep credentials server-side; no shared reader account, delegated Users Read role, or private/admin-view fallback is required. Administrative reads and approved writes still use the acting administrator's grant.

Require a successful current own-profile lookup for protected access; unavailable/hidden/deleted profiles or rejected credentials deny access with an explicit unavailable or reconnection outcome. This is a visibility/access check, not an administrator-only `suspended` status check. Verify suspended/deleted-account behavior with existing sessions in the live tenant; access denial depends on Google's credential and Directory propagation and must not be described as instantaneous suspension detection.

References: [Directory user permissions](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/v1/guides/manage-users#retrieve_a_user_as_a_non-administrator), [Directory read views](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/get), [OAuth scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/v1/guides/authorizing), [domain-wide delegation guidance](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/domain-wide-delegation-best-practices), and [existing-user password reset](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/reset-a-users-password).

# Automate account handover with a temporary password email

When an administrator accepts a signup request, the application creates the Workspace user with a throwaway password that must be changed at next sign-in. Once every selected membership has succeeded, the application resets that password to a random temporary password, again requiring a change at next sign-in, and emails it to the applicant's verified contact email through Gmail, sent as the acting administrator. This replaces the manual Admin console steps and the "confirm instructions were sent" step. Reset and mail failures leave the request awaiting the email, and an administrator can send it again from the request page.

This supersedes ADR 0001's rejection of emailing a plaintext password for the handover message, and, for this message only, ADR 0002's dedicated-mailbox sender. The acting administrator's `gmail.send` grant sends the email, so the application holds no separate mailbox credential for it.

The trade-off is honest: a temporary password travels in plaintext email. The application limits the exposure by requiring a change at first sign-in, invalidating the earlier password whenever a new one is sent, and never storing or logging the password, which is kept out of mail records and the request row. The residual risk is that someone who can read the applicant's mailbox before first sign-in can use the password. The application does not confirm delivery or sign-in; the email records only that it was sent.
EOF
